Which arm is thinking in the datacenter?

Both clips run the same policy on the same YAM arm: pick up the red lid, place it on the black box. One runs the model on the robot's own Jetson Thor. The other ships every observation to an RTX PRO 6000 in another building and back, over ordinary WiFi. Pick the remote one, then reveal.

Clip length is not a hint. These are two separate rollouts, and a policy that replans differently takes a different route to the same goal — the timing evidence is on the next slide.

How the time came down

A faster GPU only wins after the wire gets small

The remote GPU was quicker from the very first run — and remote inference still lost while every observation went out as a fresh JPEG. Moving the model off the robot is not a GPU-placement problem. It is a whole-path problem.

Starting path → today 580 → 130.7 ms 77% off the original HTTP/TCP path
Inference, Thor → RTX 169.8 → 75.5 ms 2.25× faster on the remote GPU
Observation per action 87.6 → 21.5 KB 4× smaller once H.264 replaced JPEG
